summary.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ Its ancient graph is interpreted as a handled container, though the pictured object’s name is unknown and a sound-based explanation of the shift to ‘use’ remains unverified.

formation.text: Pictographic under the bucket-and-handle interpretation: the whole graph depicts a container, with its body on the left and handle on the right. This conflicts with the received 說文 analysis as 卜 plus 中. Other accounts connect 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph, or analyze 用 as 同 with a handle added and 同 supplying sound. The competing analyses are unresolved, and no phonetic component is established.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a bucket or container, with the left side as its body and the right as a handle. This is a paleographic interpretation, not an independently checked depiction.

history.text: A catalogue indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script and 說文 forms of 用, but its text does not describe individual strokes or establish a detailed sequence of shape changes.

The bucket-and-handle reading differs from the received 說文 parsing 從卜從中. A separate account treats 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph; another parses 用 as 同 with a handle added and assigns 同 a sound role. These competing graphic analyses are unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The graph is proposed to have been borrowed from a container picture for ‘put into effect/use,’ but the pictured object’s spoken name is unknown, so the sound match cannot be verified. 用’s own pronunciations do not establish that missing name.

Oracle-bone examples show 用 in contexts indicating whether a proposed action was carried out, but the first occurrence and relative chronology of this use and the proposed container sense remain unsettled. A Qin-slip container or measure use read 桶 does not determine their order.

senses.text: 用/不用 is reported after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. This early attested use does not prove the graph’s original meaning.
One Qin-slip context is read 桶, ‘container’ or ‘measure.’ It preserves a container-related use but does not establish the graph’s original meaning or when this use arose.

senses.gloss: preposition equivalent to 以; sequential or causal conjunction
senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples include prepositional and conjunctive uses alongside the verb ‘use.’ Their relative chronology and development are not established by these examples.
用 has the common current meaning ‘use’ or ‘employ.’ The evidence does not establish a complete path from the inscriptional uses to its present range.

limitations.text: Several uses are attested, but the evidence does not establish a semantic development linking them. The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘carry out/use’ remains unverified because the object’s spoken name is unknown.

overview.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One account interprets its ancient graph as a handled container borrowed for a similar-sounding word, though the object’s name and the sound match are unknown.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a handled container. Its proposed connection to ‘use’ depends on a sound-based borrowing whose match is unknown.
